body.statement: For \(K\ge2\), \(n\ge2\), and \(1\le d\le n-1\), \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,0,s)<\infty\) iff \(s\ge d\); for \(1\le\tau\le n-2\), \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)<\infty\) iff \(s\ge\min\{d+1,n-1\}\). Also \(N^{\star}(n,K,0,\tau,s)=0\). Each necessity direction is witnessed by two legal models with \(\Delta=V\) whose complete oracles agree for every allowed target, and each sufficiency direction recovers \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\).
body.justification: The theorem identifies exactly when bounded interventions contain enough joint blocker capacity for union recovery.
body.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional proves a local size threshold but does not prove a full-oracle finite-versus-infinite minimax frontier or legal transcript indistinguishability.
body.consumer: A perturbation platform can rule out an intervention-size budget before collecting data and can identify the smallest multi-target panel size capable of exact latent-state union recovery.
